source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Two methods of covering the planting bed are illustrated: covering with plastic mulch film, and covering with rice straw/stubble mulch.

For plastic mulch film, the recommended steps shown are: (1) spread the plastic sheet flat over the bed with the shinier/reflective side facing up; (2) bury the edges and both ends of the sheet with soil to hold it firmly in place; (3) punch planting holes through the plastic using a heated tool (a metal punch or hot can/tin, ក>ុងភ្លើង) at the marked planting spots; (4) prepare and fill each planting hole with compost/soil mix before transplanting the seedling.

A measuring string or rope marked at the correct planting interval is used to mark hole positions evenly along the row before punching, so that plant-to-plant and row-to-row spacing stay consistent.

An alternative shown in the booklet is covering the bed and furrow with rice straw or stubble mulch instead of plastic film; the accompanying photos show workers laying straw over the furrows between planted rows. The training material did not provide additional text detail on this straw-mulch method beyond the photos, so specific application steps for it should be confirmed with a local extension officer.

Both mulching methods serve the same purpose noted under land preparation: reducing water runoff/erosion and suppressing weed growth around the watermelon plants.
